notes:
Summary: Veridian Serving Labs is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production serving of a multi-tenant language platform. Primary motivation is predictable unit economics and latency guarantees for paying customers. They run a mix of chat and embedding workloads; reranking used for search relevance tuning.

Key technical requirements and asks (copied from call):
- Throughput target: sustained 200 requests/sec (avg payload ~1.5k tokens), peak bursts to 600 req/sec for short windows.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 120ms for chat (2000 token cap considered), p50 < 60ms.
- Availability: target 99.95% for regional Dedicated cluster; automatic fallback to hosted variants in other region in outage.
- Security: SSO/SAML + SCIM, SOC2 + audit logs, customer-managed KMS (HSM on-prem for some customers), data residency (US/EU separation).
- Deployment: prefer VPC-private Dedicated with option to host an on-prem appliance for regulated customers.

Cost modeling notes (from internal Redwood pricing session and shared spreadsheet):
- Baseline sizing recommended: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved). Expected steady-state utilization assumption = 60% (conservative); optimistic = 80%.
- Redwood quoted committed monthly capacity price = $X (redacted). Break-even vs hosted per-token model occurs around ~180B tokens/month at conservative utilization.
- Unit economics breakdown provided to Veridian: amortized GPU + infra overhead per token, average token cost at 60% util ~ $0.00012/token vs hosted pay-as-you-go ~ $0.00035/token for same model.
- Sensitivity: if utilization dips below 40% cost per token > hosted rate; add-on burst capacity pricing and autoscale clauses discussed.

POC plan: 48h deploy of Dedicated cluster in us-east, run representative traffic replay (real token distribution). Measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, tail KV-cache hit rates, and token throughput. Engineer checklist: kernel tuning, batcher settings, KV cache warmup, sequence length caps.

Sales/Procurement asks from Veridian: clear SLA with credits table, defined maintenance windows, SLO measurement telemetry exposed in Console, and an explicit runbook for cross-region failover (need playbook for customer-facing downtime).

Quotes from stakeholders: "We need predictable unit economics — customers won't accept token bills that swing monthly. If Dedicated gives us steady cost at scale, that's the win." - Head of Product.

Open items: legal to send SLA redlines by 2026-03-20; security team to confirm HSM/KMS integration technical guide; finance to validate ARR model and procurement signoff by 2026-04. 

Attached artifacts: pricing deck link (drive), POC harness instructions (drive), security questionnaire (drive).
technical_summary: Detailed cost model focus: commit levels vs utilization. Using Redwood estimate for 4x A100-eq reserved cluster: fixed monthly commit C, variable ops and storage O. Effective cost per token = (C / (monthly_tokens * utilization_adjustment)) + O. Example assumptions provided: avg token length 15, requests/sec steady 200 -> monthly tokens ~ 200 * 3600 * 24 * 30 * 15 = ~777.6M tokens. At 60% util effective cost/token conservatively low (see notes). Also examined burst pricing: ability to send overflow to hosted with 2x cost premium. Recommended next step: run POC and capture real token/month to recompute break-even point and finalize committed tier (4 vs 6 GPUs).
sales_playbook_notes:
- Offer 3-tier committed plans (4, 6, 8 GPU buckets) with utilization guidance and explicit autoscale credit model.
- Include 'rollover' tokens or flexible top-up mechanism for seasonal spikes.
- Draft SLA with 99.95% and credit schedule; include incident runbook appendix.
- Bring in Solutions Eng to run cost sensitivity walkthrough with Veridian finance.
